p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** The practical work of shipping managed blocks: migrating an existing tool that overwrites whole files onto a block without eating its users' data, a fixture table that pins the state machine so a test suite can lock it down, and the rule for what content belongs inside the block versus in a tool-owned file it points at.

p.THE-HARDEST-CASE-IS-AN-EXISTING-OVERWRIT: The hardest case is not a new tool — it is an existing one that has been rewriting a whole file for releases, and now must become a co-tenant without a destructive flag day.

p.THE-MIGRATION-HAS-THREE-MOVING-PARTS: The migration has three moving parts.

p.A-LEGACY-FILE-CARRIES-NO-MARKERS: A file written by the old whole-file path carries **no markers** — the tool never wrote any.

p.ABSENT-CANNOT-TELL-LEGACY-FROM-FRESH: So a plain *absent* classification cannot tell a legacy file apart from a genuinely fresh host file.

p.DISTINGUISH-THEM-BY-RECOGNISING-THE-OLD-: Distinguish them by recognising the old generated content:

facts.DETECT-KNOWN-OLD-FORM-REPLACE-WITH-A-CLE: If the entire file matches the tool's **known old generated form** (match the exact header string the old version wrote — precise, so a false positive cannot destroy a hand-authored file), the content *was* the tool's. Replace it with a clean file containing just the block; nothing is lost.
facts.DETECT-OTHERWISE-TAKE-THE-ABSENT-CREATE-: Otherwise, take the ordinary **absent → create** path: append a block, preserve every other byte. A file the tool did not generate is a file with a co-tenant, even if that co-tenant is the user's past self.

p.MATCH-THE-OLD-FORM-BY-AN-EXACT-STRING: Match the old form by an **exact** string, never a loose heuristic: here a false positive means wrongly deleting a file a human wrote by hand, which is the exact disaster the whole practice exists to prevent.

p.CONVERT-ONCE-AND-GATE-IT-ON-EXPLICIT-CON: Do the legacy-to-block conversion **once**, and gate it on explicit consent when there is any doubt the file is purely tool-owned.

p.A-SILENT-CONVERSION-IS-THE-SAME-TRUST-VI: A silent in-place conversion is the same trust violation as the overwrite it replaces. Concretely:

facts.CONVERSION-ON-FIRST-RUN-CONVERT-AND-PRIN: On first run of the block-aware version, if the file is the known old form, convert and print one line saying so.
facts.CONVERSION-IF-THE-FILE-HAS-DRIFTED-DO-NO: If the file has drifted from the known form — a human touched it — do **not** guess. Take the append path, or stop and ask, depending on how destructive a wrong guess would be. When in doubt, append: a spurious extra block is a cosmetic annoyance the user can delete; a deleted hand-edit is unrecoverable.

p.OWNING-A-BLOCK-INSTEAD-OF-A-FILE-CHANGES: A tool that starts owning a block instead of a file has changed its contract with every host file on every user's machine.

p.SAY-SO-IN-THE-RELEASE-NOTES-IN-ONE-PLAIN: Say so in the release notes, in one plain sentence: *"toolname now writes into a delimited `<toolname>` block instead of replacing the whole file; your own edits outside the block are preserved from this release on."*

p.both-kinds-of-user-need-to-know: Users who hand-edited the file around the tool need to know the hazard is gone; users who scripted around the old whole-file behaviour need to know it changed.

p.THE-CLASSIFIER-IS-THE-SAFETY-CRITICAL-PA: The classifier is the safety-critical part: it decides whether a write is a splice, an append, or a hard stop.

p.PIN-EVERY-CASE-WITH-A-FIXTURE: Pin every case with a fixture.

p.FEED-EACH-FIXTURE-TO-THE-CLASSIFIER-AND-: Feed each fixture file to the classifier and assert the verdict.

td.fact: One opener, then one closer, in order
One ordered pair, but at the top of the file, preceded by user text
A closer appears before its opener
An opener with no closer (or vice versa)
An opener, another opener, then two closers
One ordered pair with nothing between
Present, and new body equals old body

p.TWO-ASSERTIONS-DESERVE-THEIR-OWN-TESTS: Two assertions deserve their own tests beyond the verdict:

facts.ASSERT-PRESERVATION-OF-EVERY-BYTE-OUTSID: **Preservation.** After a splice, every byte outside the markers is identical to the input — assert on the full file, not just the block.
facts.ASSERT-CLEAN-REMOVAL-IS-THE-IDENTITY-FUN: **Clean removal.** After a remove, the file equals what it was before the block was ever created, separation blank line included — a round-trip create-then-remove is the identity function on the surrounding content.

p.THE-MOVED-AND-NESTED-ROWS-ARE-THE-ONES-N: The moved and nested rows are the ones naive implementations get wrong: *moved* tempts a tool to "put the block back where it belongs" (never — position is the user's), and *nested* tempts a tool to match the outer pair and proceed (never — anything but one clean ordered pair is malformed).

what-belongs.title: What belongs inside the block

p.KEEP-THE-BLOCK-SMALL-STABLE-AND-POINTER-: Keep the block **small, stable, and pointer-like**.

p.the-block-is-a-window-not-storage: It is a window onto the file every reader already opens; it is not storage.

facts.GOOD-BLOCK-CONTENT: **Good block content:** a few lines that rarely change — a redirect ("read the boot manifest"), a short set of exports, a single source line, a pointer to where the real payload lives.
facts.BAD-BLOCK-CONTENT: **Bad block content:** a large, frequently regenerated payload — a hundred lines of generated config, an embedded database, anything that produces a big diff on every run.

p.PUT-A-LARGE-PAYLOAD-IN-A-TOOL-OWNED-FILE: When the payload is large, put it in a **tool-owned file** — a file with a co-tenant of exactly zero, safely under whole-file ownership (see [`rejected-designs.xml`](rejected-designs.xml#whole-file)) — and let the block hold only a pointer to it:

what-belongs.fence: <toolname> <!-- Generated by toolname — do not edit; pointer only. --> source /opt/toolname/generated.sh # the large payload lives here </toolname>

p.THE-POINTER-KEEPS-THE-SHARED-FILES-DIFFS: This keeps the shared file's diffs small and legible — the block changes only when the pointer changes — while the volatile payload churns freely in a file no human shares.

p.the-block-is-the-polite-handshake: The block is the polite handshake in the shared space; the payload lives in the tool's own room.

facts.SUM-MIGRATE-BY-RECOGNISING-THE-EXACT-OLD: Migrate by recognising the exact old generated form: known form → convert once, consent-gated; anything else → append and preserve. Match by exact string, never a heuristic.
facts.SUM-ANNOUNCE-THE-CONTRACT-CHANGE: Announce the contract change in one changelog sentence.
facts.SUM-PIN-THE-STATE-MACHINE-WITH-FIXTURES: Pin the state machine with fixtures: absent, present, moved, duplicated / reversed / lone / nested markers, empty body, byte-identical. Test preservation and clean removal separately.
facts.SUM-KEEP-THE-BLOCK-SMALL-AND-POINTER-LIK: Keep the block small and pointer-like; large payloads live in a tool-owned file the block points at.
